name: Copper peptide eye cream

lead: Copper peptide eye creams contain GHK-Cu, a naturally occurring complex of the tripeptide glycyl-histidyl-lysine with copper, listed on labels as copper tripeptide-1. Brands include it in anti-aging products aimed at fine lines and firmness.

The appearance chain proposed is: peptide supports collagen production and skin repair, so skin looks firmer. Wikipedia reports late-1980s lab findings of collagen stimulation and several small, short controlled facial studies reporting anti-wrinkle effects [1].

paras: People apply it as a cosmetic cream or serum to the skin around the eyes as part of a skincare routine, often alongside moisturizers or other serums. Results in cosmetic studies are described over weeks.
Wikipedia notes GHK-Cu raises both skin-protein-degrading enzymes and their inhibitors and suggests caution [1]. Cosmetic use is generally topical and over the counter.

chain: Proposed support of collagen and repair
Skin looks firmer, finer lines softer
angle.text: Manufacturers and users apply it hoping to firm and smooth thin eye-area skin. Small facial studies on GHK-Cu report anti-wrinkle effects.

lead: GHK-Cu is a complex of the tripeptide glycyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine with copper(II). Loren Pickart isolated it from human plasma in 1973, and its levels were reported to decline with age [1].
Cosmetic products list it as copper tripeptide-1 in anti-aging and hair products, and some brands formulate eye creams with it for the delicate eye-area skin [1].

Research includes late-1980s findings of collagen synthesis in fibroblasts, animal wound-healing studies and small controlled facial studies reporting firming and anti-wrinkle effects, which the encyclopedia describes as limited by small size and short duration [1]. A 2026 Phase 2 registration is testing a topical GHK-Cu gel on acute skin wounds [2].

paras: In cosmetics GHK-Cu appears in anti-aging products under the INCI name copper tripeptide-1 [1]. Community threads discuss formulations, for example whether a widely sold copper peptide serum is well formulated and which hyaluronic acid and copper peptide serum to buy [3][4].

A 2026 review covers GHK-Cu coordination chemistry, formulation and therapeutic evidence [5]. Microneedle-mediated delivery of copper peptide through skin has been studied in the lab [6]. Wound-healing hydrogels containing copper peptides have been reported in diabetic wound research [7].

Several controlled facial studies reported anti-aging, firming and anti-wrinkle effects, but with small samples and short durations [1]. A 2026 registered Phase 2 trial of topical GHK-Cu gel on punch-biopsy wounds (n=60) is recruiting [2]. No published trial specific to eye creams was identified.

timeline.event: Phase 2 topical GHK-Cu wound trial starts [2].
